25 Infrared laser light is used for the transmission of data along optic fibres.
What is a typical wavelength of infrared radiation?
A
5 × 10–5
m
B
5 × 10–7
m
C
2 × 10–9
m
D
2 × 10–11
m

hints: Notice the question asks for infrared, which lies just beyond the red end of visible light at about $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Recall the order of increasing wavelength is gamma, X-ray, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwave, radio, so infrared must be longer than $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
Compare each power of ten given, $10^{-5} \text{ m}$ against $10^{-7} \text{ m}$, $10^{-9} \text{ m}$ and $10^{-11} \text{ m}$, and keep only the value longer than visible light.
walkthrough: Identify the reference: visible light spans roughly $4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, with red at the long-wavelength end.
State the rule: in the electromagnetic spectrum infrared is adjacent to red with longer wavelength, roughly $10^{-6} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-3} \text{ m}$.
Check option B: $5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ is inside the visible range, so it cannot be infrared.
Check options C and D: $2 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$ and $2 \times 10^{-11} \text{ m}$ are $100$ to $10000$ times shorter than visible light, in the X-ray and gamma regions.
Check the remaining value: $5 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}$ is about $70$ times longer than red light, which fits the infrared range. This is option A.

A.explanation: Infrared has longer wavelength than red light at about $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, so $5 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}$ is a typical infrared value.

B.explanation: $5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ is $500 \text{ nm}$, which is green visible light, not infrared.

C.explanation: $2 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$ is much too short and lies in the X-ray region, not infrared.

D.explanation: $2 \times 10^{-11} \text{ m}$ is much too short and lies in the gamma-ray region, not infrared.
